title: The Prefix un-
keyIdea: un- is a prefix: a small part that goes at the front of a word and changes what it means. With a describing word, un- means not: unhappy means not happy, unfair means not fair. With a doing word, un- undoes the job: unlock opens what lock shut, untie undoes a bow. To spell it, write un and then the whole word with no gap and no letters changed. Some words just start with u and n, like under and uncle; take off un and no word is left, so they have no prefix.
familyTip: Play 'flip it' at home. You say a word, such as happy, kind, tidy or zip, and your child adds un- and says what the new word means: unzip opens the zip. Then write two of them together, saying 'un, then the whole word'. If they say unbig or unsad, laugh together and find the real opposite: small, happy.

visual.caption: Does un- mean not, or does it undo a job? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: put un- at the front, match un- words to pictures, spell them, spot words that only start with un, and fill sentence gaps.

kid: un is a small part we put at the front of a word. It is called a prefix. It changes what the word means.
Put un in front of happy. Now you have unhappy. It means not happy. unkind means not kind. unfair means not fair.
un can undo a job too. You lock the door. Then you unlock it, and it opens. You tie a bow. Then you untie it.
To spell it, write u, n, then the word. Do not change the word. No gap. Be careful: under and uncle just start with u and n. Take off un and no word is left.
adult: Ages 5 to 6. The National Curriculum in England lists the prefix un- in Year 1 spelling (English Appendix 1: 'The prefix un- is added at the beginning of a word without any change to the spelling of the root word', with unhappy, undo, unload, unfair and unlock as examples). Reading the same words is part of Year 1 word reading, and Common Core L.1.4b and L.2.4b use affixes as clues to word meaning.

un- does two jobs. On an adjective it means not (unhappy, unkind, untidy, unwell). On a verb it reverses the action (unlock, untie, unzip, unpack, undo). It is a prefix because it comes before the root word, and the root keeps every letter, so unnecessary has two n's only because necessary starts with n.

Common mistakes: putting the prefix after the word (happyun), leaving a gap (un happy), dropping or doubling a root letter (unhapy, unzipp), writing on- for un-, reading un- as 'very' or 'again', and treating any word that starts with u-n (under, uncle, unicorn) as un- plus a word. Children also invent words such as unbig; not every word takes un-, and the opposite of big is small.

In the lab your child drags un- to the front of four describing words, taps the picture that shows unlock, untie, unzip and unpack, picks the right spelling of four un- words, sorts six words by taking un off to see if a real word is left, and fills four sentence gaps where one gap needs the plain word kind.

practice.hint: un- in front of a describing word means not.
practice.explain: un + fair = unfair, which means not fair.

practice.prompt: A word has {h} letters. You put un- in front of it. How many letters does the new word have?
practice.hint: un adds two letters, u and n, and the word stays the same.
practice.explain: The word keeps all {h} letters and un adds 2, so {=h+2} letters.

practice.hint: Write u, n, then the word, with no gap.
practice.explain: un joins straight onto lock: unlock.

practice.prompt: Ali ties {t} bows. Then he unties {u} of them. How many bows are still tied?
practice.hint: untie undoes tie, so each one he unties is not tied any more.
practice.explain: {t} tied take away {u} untied leaves {=t-u} still tied.

practice.prompt: Which word has the prefix un-?
practice.hint: Take off un. Is a real word left?
practice.explain: untidy is un + tidy. Take un off under or uncle and no word is left.

pool.prompt: What do you do when you unpack a bag?
pool.hint: un- undoes the job. What does pack do?
pool.explain: Packing puts things in, so unpacking undoes it: you take things out.

choices: at the front of the word
at the end of the word
in the middle of the word
pool.hint: un- is a prefix. Pre means before.
pool.explain: A prefix goes before the word: un + kind = unkind.

pool.prompt: The cat is not well. The cat is ...
pool.hint: not well needs un- at the front.
pool.explain: unwell means not well, with un- at the front.

pool.prompt: There are {a} zips done up on the bags. Mia unzips {b}. How many are still done up?
pool.hint: Each one she unzips is open now.
pool.explain: {a} done up take away {b} opened leaves {=a-b}.

pool.hint: Keep every letter of kind and leave no gap.
pool.explain: un + kind = unkind, with kind spelt just the same.

pool.prompt: Why is under NOT an un- word?
choices: Take off un and der is not a word
It has an e in it
pool.hint: Take off un. What is left?
pool.explain: Take un off under and der is left, which is not a word. unfair leaves fair, so it has the prefix.

pool.prompt: A list has {k} words like kind, fair and tidy. Sam adds un- to each one. How many un- words does he make?
pool.hint: One un- word for each word on the list.
pool.explain: Each word gives one un- word, so {k}.

pool.prompt: Gran helps me tie my shoes. That is ...
pool.hint: Is helping a nice thing to do?
pool.explain: Helping is nice, so it is kind. unkind would mean not kind, and unhelp is not a word.

pool.prompt: You undo your coat button. What happens?
pool.hint: undo undoes do. What did doing up the button do?
pool.explain: un- undoes the job, so the button comes open.

pool.hint: un- goes at the front and means not.
pool.explain: untidy means not tidy. un- goes at the front.
